_readme: ADVERSARIAL SEED for the Surveys group. TEMPORARY - deleted in Step 08.
Explicit long primary keys throughout (Rule 1). Applied with SET IDENTITY_INSERT, which needs
no production source change. Same salt + same long => same hash id, so a seeded id compares
LITERALLY and a wrong id is a diff rather than noise. Never let the database pick these.
ID BLOCKS, chosen so that no row's PK ever equals a foreign id it carries. That is deliberate:
trap 2 is a link row's own PK leaking into a child's ID, and it is INVISIBLE if the two numbers
happen to coincide.
Survey          5_000_00x
SurveyVersion   5_100_00x
SurveyInstance  5_200_00x
SurveyResponse  5_300_00x
SurveyAnswer    5_400_00x   <- link row; PK deliberately far from SurveyResponseID
BankQuestion    5_500_00x
ScreenTemplate  5_600_00x
WHICH TRAPS THIS GROUP ACTUALLY HAS - verified against the code, then adversarially re-checked.
Two of the four do not exist here, and are NOT faked:
trap3write  PRESENT, confirmed. Survey.PublishedVersionNumber is dropped on the DTO->entity
map (GeneralMappingProfile.cs:41-42) because the publish flow derives it. Seeded
as 7 on survey 5000001: a create/update body sends a different value, so if the
generated mapper starts writing it by convention the readback shows the client's
number instead of the derived one.
trap3write  PRESENT, narrower than first claimed. BankQuestion.Locked (GeneralMappingProfile
.cs:75) is ignored on the reverse map; seeded true on 5500001 so a body sending
false must NOT flip it.
trap1       ABSENT in its literal form. There is no .ForViewChildren/.ForView child predicate
anywhere in this group and no child-entity array on any DTO. Soft-deleted rows are
still seeded below, because the framework's global IsDeleted filter is a different
mechanism worth watching and costs nothing to cover.
trap2       ABSENT today. SurveyAnswer IS link-shaped (own PK + SurveyResponseID + BankEntryID)
but nothing projects its PK into a child's ID. It is seeded with deliberately
divergent numbers anyway - the point of a trap-shaped row is to catch the trap
being INTRODUCED by the upgrade, not only to reproduce one that exists now.
trap3read   ABSENT. Every .Ignore() in this group is on the DTO->entity direction.
Rows carrying _marker are the ones the summary gate checks for literally in list bodies. That
gate replaces '> 0 rows', which a sample host's own demo seed satisfies on its own and which
therefore cannot distinguish 'the adversarial seed was applied' from 'only demo data is here'.
Keys beginning with _ are harness metadata and are never written to SQL.
TABLE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: rows are inserted in the order listed, so a table must appear
after every table it has a foreign key into. BankQuestion precedes SurveyAnswer because
SurveyAnswer.BankEntryID has an FK to BankQuestion.BankEntryID.
JSON-COLUMN VALUES MUST BE REAL DTOs, not {}. QuestionJson deserializes into the
polymorphic QuestionDto (discriminator property 'type'), and TemplateJson into
ScreenTemplateDto. A bare {} yields null and GET {id} then throws 500 inside the
mapper - which is a seed defect masquerading as an endpoint failure.

rows._why: PublishedVersionNumber = 7 is a REPOSITORY-DERIVED value the reverse map ignores. A write body sending a different number must not change it.
rows.Name: PARITY-SURVEY-TRAP3WRITE derived-published-version

rows._why: An ordinary row, so a diff on the hostile row can be told apart from a diff affecting every row.
rows.Name: PARITY-SURVEY-PLAIN control row

rows._why: Soft-deleted. Must NEVER appear in a list body. If it does, the global IsDeleted query filter regressed. Deliberately has no _marker - its absence is the assertion.
rows.Name: PARITY-SURVEY-SOFTDELETED must-not-appear

rows._why: The published snapshot survey 5000001's PublishedVersionNumber=7 refers to. PK 5100001 differs from SurveyID 5000001 on purpose.

Owns two responses, one of them soft-deleted. Any response-derived aggregate on this instance must count ONE, not two. This is the aggregate form of trap 1 - the literal child-array form does not exist in this group.
Live response on instance 5200001. PK 5300001 differs from SurveyInstanceID 5200001 on purpose.
SOFT-DELETED sibling on the same instance. This is the row that makes the aggregate trap fire: a count that includes it has lost the IsDeleted predicate.

Locked = true is ignored on the DTO->entity map (GeneralMappingProfile.cs:75). A write body sending locked=false must NOT flip it. Locked also arms the repository's own immutability guards, so a regression here changes behaviour, not just a displayed flag. QuestionJson carries a REAL polymorphic QuestionDto with its 'type' discriminator: a bare {} deserializes to null and makes GET {id} throw AutoMapperMappingException 500, which the first capture caught.
Control: same shape, Locked false, so a diff on the locked row is attributable.

LINK ROW. Its own PK (5400001) is deliberately far from both foreign ids it carries (SurveyResponseID 5300001, BankEntryID a fixed Guid). No mapping leaks it today, so this row is a GUARD: if the upgrade introduces a projection that emits the link PK where a child id belongs, the wrong number shows up here and nowhere else.
Plain row so the ScreenTemplate triple's list and detail bodies are non-empty. An empty list body is a case that cannot fail.
